channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Patrimônio de Lula diminui 35%, com gasto de R$ 2,2 mi da aposentadoria
item.description: The personal wealth of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva decreased by 35% over his four-year term, dropping from R$ 7.42 million to R$ 4.78 million, according to the asset declaration submitted to the TSE. The decline was mainly due to R$ 2.2 million in expenditures from his pension.

item.title: Lula: nenhum banqueiro da Faria Lima ou ruralista sabe o que é acordar com rato nadando em casa
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized Faria Lima bankers and ruralists for not understanding the reality of floods and the daily struggles of poor people, saying they don’t know what it’s like to wake up with a rat swimming in their home. He argued that those who set interest rates and defend fiscal adjustment are disconnected from how ordinary Brazilians live.

item.title: Dois retratos revelam o paradoxo da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro announced Alfredo Gaspar as his running mate in a sparsely attended event, underscoring his weakness in party alliance-building, as he failed to secure support from Centrão-aligned parties. Nevertheless, recent polls show a narrowing gap with Lula, with Bolsonaro gaining traction among independent voters, preserving his competitiveness despite lacking formal party backing.

item.title: Flávio acena ao eleitorado feminino e fala em indicar mulheres ao STF
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) reached out to female voters in Itapetininga, promising to appoint both men and women to the Supreme Federal Court if elected. He emphasized gender balance on the Court as part of his 2026 campaign strategy to gain support among women.

item.title: Flávio critica contas de Lula e promete Brasil entre as 7 maiores economias
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL party's presidential candidate, criticized Lula's government indebtedness and pledged to balance public accounts, restore investor confidence, and bring Brazil into the world's top seven economies by the end of his potential term. He denounced the 'leftist mindset' as a 'cancer of Brazil' and called the election decisive for the nation's future, while also proposing policies to support women entrepreneurs, including expanding microcredit access and doubling the number of female business owners.

item.title: Lula declara R$ 4,7 milhões em patrimônio ao TSE, valor 35% menor em relação a 2022
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva declared R$ 4.7 million in assets to the TSE for the 2026 elections, a 35% decrease from R$ 7.4 million in 2022. The bulk of his wealth is in private pension plans (R$ 3.3 million), followed by real estate (R$ 739,200) and financial investments (R$ 454,200). The decline is primarily due to a R$ 2.7 million reduction in VGBL pension plans.

item.title: Em evento do MTST, Lula critica Faria Lima e cobranças por ajuste fiscal e pressiona por fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Lula criticized interest rates and market demands for fiscal adjustment, accusing elites of not understanding the reality of the poor. Speaking at an MTST event in Taboão da Serra, he urged the public to study Brazilian presidential history to recognize his commitment to social inclusion, while Boulos highlighted Minha Casa, Minha Vida projects and attacked Bolsonaro for ending the program.

item.title: Flávio critica decisão de Moraes que barrou visita a Bolsonaro no Dia dos Pais
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro criticized Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to block a visit by his brothers Carlos and Jair Renan to their father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, on Father's Day, claiming it deprives a father of the right to embrace his children. The ruling upholds a 30-day suspension of visits, allowing only medical, physiotherapeutic, and legal meetings, following Bolsonaro's breach of court-imposed conditions, including Flávio's social media publication of a letter from the former president.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro fala em indicar mulheres ao STF em evento com aliadas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL party's presidential candidate, again criticized Supreme Court (STF) ministers during a campaign event in the interior of São Paulo. Seeking to appeal to female voters, he stated that, if elected, he would appoint 'men and women' to the Court, combining his conservative agenda with an effort to broaden support among women.

item.title: Em SP, Lula usa evento do MTST para exaltar Haddad e Simone Tebet
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva used the 30th-anniversary event of the MTST in Taboão da Serra to praise his government's economic policy, highlight the income tax exemption for those earning up to R$5,000, and claim Brazil has the lowest four-year accumulated inflation in its history. He also lauded Fernando Haddad as the author of the IR exemption project and Simone Tebet for her courage in moving to São Paulo to run for Senate, emphasizing the importance of women's participation in politics.

item.title: Campanha da ‘Católicas pelo Direito de Decidir’ recoloca aborto no debate em ano eleitoral
item.description: The organization Catholics for the Right to Decide launches the 'Safe to Decide' campaign, featuring anonymous testimonies from women who have undergone abortion, to expand the debate on abortion in Brazil during the 2026 election year. The initiative aims to highlight real women’s experiences and push for reform of current restrictive abortion laws.

item.title: Lula: anunciamos o menor desmatamento da década na Amazônia
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced he will send data on the lowest deforestation rate in a decade in the Amazon to the United States, aiming to correct what he claims are false reports previously given to former President Donald Trump. He emphasized that Brazil is making real progress in environmental preservation and that the truth should be known internationally.

item.title: Os números das pesquisas Quaest, Meio/Ideia e BTG/Nexus sobre a disputa Lula x Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Quaest, Meio/Ideia, and BTG/Nexus polls show Lula leading the 2026 presidential race in the first round, with advantages ranging from 4 to 9 points over Flávio Bolsonaro. In the second-round simulations, the gap narrows to between 1 and 5.5 points, with BTG/Nexus showing the tightest contest at 46% to 45%, technically tied within the margin of error.

item.title: Vídeo de IA de Bolsonaro: seis em cada dez brasileiros desconhecem o tema, diz Genial/Quaest
item.description: Genial/Quaest survey shows 60% of Brazilians are unaware of the AI-generated video featuring Jair Bolsonaro's image and voice, used at the PL convention to support Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 presidential campaign. Even among Bolsonaro family supporters, 55% did not know about the AI use. Half of voters see the AI use as problematic, while 43% do not consider it irregular.

item.title: Flávio promete classificar facções como terroristas e "recuperar territórios"
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) stated that if elected in 2026, he will classify Rio de Janeiro's criminal factions (Red Command and PCC) as terrorists and 'recover territories' under their control, declaring a 'war on narcotrafficking'. The pledge was made at an event with women in Itapetininga (SP), citing Senate candidate Guilherme Derrite (PL-SP) as an ally in a hardline approach to organized crime. He also said he will say a prayer before his inauguration and aims to 'expel these demons' from the Three Powers Plaza, criticizing the federal government and judiciary.

item.title: Roberto Reis na Crusoé: O voto do cansaço
item.description: The article argues that the main electoral force in Brazil's 2026 election is not a candidate, but antipetismo — voter fatigue with the PT's political model, which has returned stronger than ever. Though unnamed, this force has a clear target: weariness with lulismo, regardless of whether Lula's opponent is Flávio Dino or another figure. The 'vote of exhaustion' is portrayed as a silent but decisive driver of the upcoming election.

item.title: Lula diz que prepara dados para “amigo Trump” sobre desmatamento
item.description: Lula says he is preparing data to show Donald Trump the reduction in Amazon deforestation, amid rising trade tensions after the U.S. raised tariffs on Brazilian goods. He aims to use Brazil’s environmental progress as leverage in trade negotiations, advocating dialogue and highlighting the revival of the PPCDAm plan as evidence of his commitment to forest preservation.

item.title: Em evento do MTST, Lula volta a criticar bancos por burocracia
item.description: President Lula criticized banking bureaucracy hindering access to government credit lines, particularly the Move Brasil program financing motorcycles for app-based delivery workers and vehicles for Uber and taxi drivers. He noted that despite good intentions, beneficiaries face excessive requirements and impossible documentation, such as unregistered land blocking housing loans. The remarks were made at the 30th anniversary event of the MTST in Taboão da Serra, attended by PT allies including Guilherme Boulos, Fernando Haddad, Simone Tebet, and Marina Silva, underscoring the party’s electoral campaign in São Paulo.

item.title: Ao lado de Lula, Janja volta a pedir banimento do Discord no Brasil
item.description: First Lady Janja da Silva renewed her call to ban Discord in Brazil during an event with the Homeless Workers' Movement (MTST) alongside President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. She argued the platform fails to protect children and adolescents and urged Lula to take action to remove it from the country.

item.title: Ao lado de Lula, Boulos adota discurso do ‘nós contra eles’ em evento do MTST
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos (PSOL), alongside President Lula, spoke at an MTST event in Taboão da Serra (SP), adopting a 'us vs them' rhetoric defending national sovereignty, dignified housing, and women's rights. He criticized Michel Temer for carrying out a coup and ending the Minha Casa Minha Vida program, and labeled Jair Bolsonaro as 'bad thing' for halting low-income housing construction. Boulos also announced new MCMV housing projects in the São Paulo metropolitan region and reaffirmed his political roots in the MTST movement.

item.title: Lula oficializa candidatura à Presidência no TSE e registra queda nos bens
item.description: Lula officially registered his re-election bid with the TSE, declaring assets of R$ 4.78 million — a 35.68% decrease from 2022. He appeared on the ballot photo wearing a straw hat, explaining it was to cover a dressing after preventive radiotherapy for skin cancer. The TSE permits such accessories if they do not hinder identification.

item.title: Moraes nega pedido para filhos visitarem Bolsonaro no Dia dos Pais
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes rejected Jair Bolsonaro's request for his sons Flávio, Carlos, and Jair Renan to visit him under house arrest on Father's Day. The defense had argued the visit should be granted as an exceptional circumstance due to the holiday. The ruling upholds existing restrictions on Bolsonaro related to ongoing investigations, including Operation Car Wash and other inquiries.

item.title: Moraes toma decisão sobre pedido de Bolsonaro para receber filhos no Dia dos Pais
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied the request by Jair Bolsonaro's defense to allow him to receive his children on Father's Day, upholding a 30-day suspension on non-essential visits. The decision followed Bolsonaro's violation of judicial restrictions after his son Flávio read a letter written by the former president on social media. The ruling aims to enforce compliance with court orders imposed on Bolsonaro due to his prior conduct.

item.title: Moraes nega pedido de defesa de Bolsonaro para receber visita de filhos no Dia dos Pais
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied Jair Bolsonaro's defense request to receive visits from his children on Father's Day, maintaining the suspension of non-medical, non-physiotherapeutic, and non-lawyer visits for 30 days. The decision reiterates that the restriction was prompted by Flávio Bolsonaro's public sharing of a handwritten letter on social media, which Moraes views as a violation of the ban on the former president's use of digital platforms. Flávio had read the letter during a live broadcast, in which Bolsonaro portrayed him as his 'spokesperson' and the best option to free Brazil from corruption, violence, and impoverishment.

item.title: Lula chama Trump de 'meu amigo' e diz querer mostrar a ele queda no desmatamento
item.description: Lula referred to Trump as 'my friend' and said he will send updated data on the decline in Amazon deforestation to correct what he claims are false premises behind the U.S. 25% tariff on Brazilian goods. He noted that deforestation alerts in the Amazon dropped 36% from August 2025 to July 2026, reaching the lowest level since 2016, according to Inpe, and intends to show Trump that allegations of illegal deforestation are unfounded.

item.title: Moraes nega visitas a Jair Bolsonaro no Dia dos Pais
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes denied a request for visits to former President Jair Bolsonaro on Father's Day, upholding a 30-day suspension of visits issued on July 17. The decision stems from Bolsonaro's violation of the ban on disseminating political-electoral manifestos through third parties, after Senator Flávio Bolsonaro read a letter on his behalf. During this period, Bolsonaro is only permitted to receive medical care, physiotherapy, and lawyer visits.

item.title: Remo x Atlético-MG no Brasileirão: onde assistir, horário e escalações
item.description: Remo and Atlético-MG face off this Saturday, the 8th, at 6:30 PM Brasília time, in the 22nd round of the Brasileirão Série A at Mangueirão Stadium in Belém. Remo, sitting in the relegation zone with 21 points, desperately needs a win to escape the bottom four, while Atlético-MG, with 28 points and coming off a Copa do Brasil quarterfinal berth, aims to climb the table. The match will be exclusively broadcast on Premiere, with confirmed lineups and referee assignments.

item.title: Três Poderes: Durigan é o vencedor da semana e ex-assessor de Lula, o perdedor
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan was named the week's winner for advocating fiscal responsibility in Lula's government program, resisting PT pressure for increased public spending. His stance reinforced a balance between social demands and economic sustainability, despite internal resistance from the governing coalition.

item.title: Vídeo de IA de Jair Bolsonaro: maioria dos brasileiros ignora o tema, aponta Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows that 60% of Brazilians are unaware of the AI-generated video of Jair Bolsonaro displayed at the PL convention, including 55% of Bolsonaro supporters. Public opinion is split: 50% view the use of AI to create Bolsonaro’s speeches as problematic, while 43% do not. Women are significantly less informed (70% unaware) compared to men (48% unaware).

item.title: Moraes proíbe que Flávio, Carlos e Jair Renan visitem Bolsonaro no Dia dos Pais
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes denied Bolsonaro's defense request for a Father's Day visit from his sons Flávio, Carlos, and Jair Renan, upholding a 30-day suspension on visits due to Bolsonaro's violation of precautionary measures. The ruling permits only medical, physiotherapeutic, and lawyer meetings during this period.

item.title: Caso Lulinha ganha força nas redes e vira munição eleitoral da oposição
item.description: The case involving Lulinha, President Lula's son, initially had less social media impact than the tariff hike and the Jaques Wagner case, but gained strength over time, becoming electoral ammunition used by the opposition. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: O patrimônio de Tarcísio de Freitas declarado à Justiça Eleitoral
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, running for re-election in São Paulo, declared R$ 2.7 million in assets to the Electoral Justice, an increase of approximately R$ 400 thousand compared to the R$ 2.3 million he declared in 2022 when he was first elected. His main assets include a savings account of R$ 525.6 thousand, fixed-income investments of R$ 33 thousand, a second savings account of R$ 500, and a Brasília property valued at R$ 2.1 million. He is running with Felicio Ramuth as his vice-presidential candidate.

item.title: Jingles para presidente de 2026 têm funk de Lula, sertanejo de Flávio, rocknejo de Renan e pop de Caiado
item.description: The first jingles for the 2026 presidential campaign have been released, with Lula using 1990s funk to highlight his journey of overcoming adversity, Flávio Bolsonaro opting for university sertanejo centered on faith, Renan Santos employing rocknejo as a response to 'Lula Lá', and Ronaldo Caiado using pop focused on combating crime. Romeu Zema is the only one among the five top candidates in the Quaest poll who has not yet released a jingle. The songs reflect each campaign’s communication strategy, aiming to connect with specific voter segments.

item.title: Moraes rejeita pedido da defesa de Bolsonaro para receber visitas de filhos no dia dos pais
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes rejected a request by Jair Bolsonaro's defense team for the former president to receive visits from his children on Father's Day, Sunday, June 9. The ruling upholds existing restrictions on Bolsonaro related to ongoing cases before the Court.

item.title: PT registra no TSE candidatura de Lula à reeleição para a Presidência, com Alckmin como vice
item.description: The PT filed with the TSE the registration request for the Lula-Alckmin ticket seeking re-election in 2026, under number 13, backed by the coalition Brasil Pronto pra Mais, which includes seven parties. The documentation was submitted at 11:20 p.m. on Friday (7) and includes the DRAP and individual candidacy requests, though it remains pending electoral court approval. The ticket repeats the 2022 winning alliance and presents an 84-page government plan emphasizing national sovereignty, parliamentary amendment reforms, ending the 6x1 work scale, and expanding health, education, and public safety policies.

item.title: Renan Santos promete acabar com as bets; o que está de fato em jogo
item.description: Renan Santos, candidate of the Missão party for Presidency, vowed to ban betting houses (bets) after sharing a follower's testimony about losing money, going into debt, and having suicidal thoughts due to gambling addiction. He argues the social costs of addiction, indebtedness, and mental health damage justify a radical measure. However, banning bets would dismantle a legalized and taxed market that, in the first four months of 2026, generated R$12.2 billion in revenue and R$4.5 billion in taxes, while also funding much of Brazil’s sports advertising.

item.title: Em programa de governo, Lula cita defesa da democracia, da soberania, regulação de redes e pede debate sobre emendas
item.description: The Lula-Alckmin 2026 government program emphasizes defending democracy, national sovereignty, regulating social media, and debating parliamentary amendments. It also proposes political reform, democratizing the public budget, criticizing high interest rates, strengthening the defense industry, and promoting diversified international cooperation while opposing liberal-conservative agendas.

item.title: Prévia de plano de Tarcísio tem dez eixos e não menciona privatizações
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas released a preview of his re-election government plan featuring ten strategic objectives, notably omitting any mention of privatizations despite their prominence in his first term. The 'Trilhas da Prosperidade' plan covers security, health, education, and the knowledge economy, and must be filed with electoral justice by August 15. It is coordinated by Natália Resende, Environment Secretary and key figure in the Sabesp privatization process.

item.title: TCU livra Janja de mais um processo envolvendo gastos em viagem internacional
item.description: The Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) dismissed an investigation into alleged irregularities in the international travel expenses of First Lady Janja during her trip to Russia, which occurred five days before President Lula’s official visit. The ruling states that Janja’s activities, even if including tourist visits, fulfill her representative and symbolic role in the Brazilian government, thereby justifying public spending. The investigation had been requested by the Chamber of Deputies’ Committee on Foreign Relations and National Defense.

item.title: No Senado, Flávio Bolsonaro apoiou cortes de impostos, mas deixou rigor fiscal de lado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a 2026 presidential candidate, promotes fiscal responsibility and tax cuts in his campaign, but his Senate record shows support for measures that weakened fiscal discipline, such as the PEC dos Precatórios and the PEC Kamikaze. While advocating for tax reduction and structural reforms, he also approved increases in social transfers and sector-specific tax benefits, contradicting his current fiscal adjustment stance.

item.title: O que diz o plano de governo de Lula divulgado pelo PT
item.description: The PT's 2026 government plan proposes revising the parliamentary amendments system, viewed as distorted and inefficient, advocating democratic regulation to improve public resource allocation. It also emphasizes defending national sovereignty across multiple dimensions — including technological, energy, environmental, and economic — and calls for regulating social media to combat disinformation and hate speech.

item.title: Plano de Lula prevê maior regulação das redes e conselho para ‘soberania digital’
item.description: The PT unveiled its government plan for Lula's fourth term, proposing increased regulation of social media and the establishment of a National Council for Digital Sovereignty. The document calls for 'democratic regulation' of digital platforms to combat misinformation and strengthen Brazil's technological autonomy.

item.title: Americanos, dívidas e eleição (por André Gustavo Stumpf)
item.description: U.S. pressures against the Brazilian government, led by Trump and his allies, create diplomatic tension without solid justification, including the withdrawal of credentials from Brazil’s ambassador in the U.S. and demands for Latin American alignment with Washington’s foreign policy, distancing the region from China. Meanwhile, the Lula government adopts short-term populist measures — such as debt renegotiation, cooking gas subsidies, and low-interest housing loans — to gain electoral support, despite knowing these policies increase public debt and strain the budget, reflecting a historical PT pattern of raising expenditures without matching revenue increases.

item.title: Promessa jamais cumprida por Lula, Autoridade Climática fica de fora de novo programa
item.description: The National Climate Authority, promised by Lula during his 2022 campaign, was excluded from the government program registered with the TSE on August 7, 2026, despite being a key demand of environmentalists and social movements. The omission draws criticism for violating an electoral pledge and weakening the government’s climate agenda. Although the program was filed on Friday, the absence of the climate authority remains a point of contention between allies and opposition.

item.title: Vice de Flávio votou pelo fim da escala 6x1 que o senador tenta barrar
item.description: Federal Deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), running mate of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), voted in favor of the PEC proposing the end of the 6x1 work schedule, opposing the senator’s public stance against the measure. While Bolsonaro seeks to block the proposal, his vice-presidential running mate supported it, revealing an internal split within the party over labor reform.

item.title: PT divulga plano de governo de Lula com defesa de soberania em resposta a Trump, arcabouço fiscal e promessa de rever emendas
item.description: The PT released Lula's 2026 re-election government plan, emphasizing national sovereignty in response to Trump, maintaining the fiscal framework, and revising parliamentary amendments labeled as a distortion totaling R$50 billion in 2026. The plan prioritizes boosting public and private investment in logistics, social infrastructure, innovation, and industry, paired with a macroeconomic policy of fiscal responsibility, declining interest rates, and controlled inflation. The 84-page, 13-chapter document has not yet been formally registered with the TSE and allows for amendments during the campaign.

item.title: Mendonça manda PT entregar documentos do congresso da sigla e do projeto Porta-Vozes de Lula
item.description: Minister André Mendonça of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ordered the Brazil of Hope Federation (PT, PCdoB and PV) to submit documents and financial proof regarding the 8th National Congress of the PT and the 'Porta-Vozes de Lula' project. The order aims to verify the legality of party acts and the use of public or private resources in the electoral context.

item.title: Mendonça vê risco de ‘contratação disfarçada de militância’ em projeto do PT
item.description: Minister André Mendonça of the TSE described the use of missions, scoring, and ranking in the PT's 'Porta-Vozes do Lula' project as 'juridically sensitive,' ordering the party to submit the initiative's rules and details on any benefits to militants. The decision partially grants a representation alleging the risk of 'disguised hiring of militants'.

item.title: Sem apostar em nenhum candidato à Presidência, Centrão prioriza disputa ao Congresso
item.description: Major centrist parties (União Brasil, PP, Republicanos, MDB, Podemos, and PSDB) have chosen to remain neutral in the first round of the 2026 presidential election, focusing instead on congressional races. These parties control 43% of congressional seats, nearly half of the Electoral Fund, and about 40% of TV and radio airtime, making their neutrality a strategically significant move. This is unprecedented in recent history: in 2022 only the PSD acted similarly, while now the same PSD is running its own candidate (Ronaldo Caiado) without attracting allies.

item.title: Corrupção é espinho no pé dos candidatos favoritos ao Planalto
item.description: Corruption is the second most concerning issue for Brazilian voters, trailing only public safety. With the Federal Police conducting investigations that touch the campaigns of the two leading presidential candidates — Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro — the race is shaping into a zero-sum confrontation, where any advantage for one comes at the expense of the other.
